parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خاتون (hâtûn), from Old Anatolian Turkish خاتون (ḫātūn), from Proto-Turkic *xātun, borrowed from Sogdian 𐼶𐼰𐽂𐼴𐼻 (xʾtwn), borrowed from Khotanese *hvatunä, *hvatuña, from Proto-Iranian *hwatā́wHniH. Cognate with Chagatai خاتون (xʾtwn). Doublet of kadın.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوچماق (uçmaq), from Old Anatolian Turkish اوچماق (uçmaq), واچماغ (uçmağ), from Proto-Turkic *uštmag, from Sogdian [script needed] (ʼwštmʼχ, “paradise”). Sogdian borrowing underwent a semantic merge with uçmak (“to fly, rise”), thence the parallels. Cognate with Kazakh
